title: Region selector: percentile-drift detector + weighted network-health index
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see suboptimal region choices when transient network flaps or slow drift in tail latency occur. Current region ranking uses simple percentile thresholds which (a) overreact to short-lived spikes and (b) miss gradual regressions in p95 relative to historical baselines. Goal: implement a composite scoring function that combines percentile drift detection (p50/p95), normalized latency percentiles, and a separate network health index (packet loss, connection errors, tcp RTT variance). The selector must be smooth (hysteresis + hold windows), support per-tenant tiering (e.g., hosted vs dedicated), and enable automated fallbacks to compatible model variants when region score degrades below a safety threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Composite region score computed every 10s using rolling 5m/1h baselines and exposed via telemetry
Region selection reduces misrouted requests (as measured by 10-day baseline PRB) by >= 30% in simulated drift scenarios
Hysteresis prevents region switching for transient spikes: a region flip requires score delta > 0.12 sustained for 30s
Automatic fallback to pre-configured model variant occurs when composite score < 0.25 and persists for 60s
New Grafana dashboard shows per-region p50/p95, z-score of p95 vs hourly baseline, network_health components, and selected region decisions
E2E canary (1% traffic) shows no >5% increase in overall latency or token-cost regressions vs control
design_decisions: Telemetry windows: short-term = 5m rolling, medium-term baseline = 1h EWMA by default; both stored as time-series in metrics store
Percentile drift detector: compute z = (current_p95 - baseline_p95_mean) / baseline_p95_std where baseline uses EWMA; clip z to [-4,4] before normalization
Latency component normalization: map p50 and p95 to 0..1 using learned per-model quantiles (10th-90th) to be robust across model sizes
Network health index = weighted_sum( packet_loss_rate, tcp_rtt_variance_norm, connection_error_rate ); weights: 0.5, 0.3, 0.2 (tunable via feature flag)
Composite score = w_lat*(0.6*norm_p95 + 0.4*norm_p50) + w_drift*norm_z + w_net*(1 - net_health_index); base weights w_lat=0.6,w_drift=0.25,w_net=0.15
Hysteresis and circuit-breaker: require sustained breach windows; implement per-route counters and per-region cooldown to avoid oscillation
Model variant compatibility: variants must declare latency/quality profile; routing will prefer same-variant if region score >= 0.3, otherwise fallback to lighter quantized variant if available
Rollout via feature-flagged canary and safe rollback path; telemetry gating enforces no regressions beyond thresholds
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Dry run: compute composite scores in parallel and record decision logs for 48h without changing routing (run in simulation mode)
Stage 1 - Canary (1% of traffic): enable selector for non-critical API keys behind feature flag; monitor key metrics for 72h
Stage 2 - Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with at least 48h observation at each step and automatic rollback triggers
Stage 3 - Tiered enablement: enable for dedicated customers in isolated pools first, then hosted; respect customer opt-outs
Stage 4 - Post-rollout: 30-day watch, collect regressions, tune weights and thresholds into Optimize recommendations
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization boundaries (edge cases and clipped z-values)
Integration tests: simulated multi-region traces with scripted p95 drift and packet loss to validate decision outcome
Chaos test: introduce packet loss and delay on one region in staging clusters and ensure selector falls back as expected and respects cooldown
Load test: confirm scoring compute adds <3% CPU overhead on routing plane at 10k req/s per region
A/B experiment for quality impact comparing fallback-to-variant vs cross-region routing for high-tier customers
